messages.subject: Reading Month/Year data
parts:
I am new to R (as you can probably guess) and I am trying to import some simple data from Excel:

1]  myDate   datapoint1  datapoint2...
2]  07/2012      1.0             1.5   ...
3]  08/2012      1.4             6.9
.
.
.

So essentially month/year.  Using read.xlsx directly interprets myDate as a factor.  I can use read.xlsx2 and specify the colClasses as "Date"

mydataframe2 <- read.xlsx2(workbook2, 1, colClasses=c("Date",rep("numeric",5)))

Read.xlsx2 then correctly recognizes the data as "date" data, but can't seem to parse the month/year formatting:

> str(mydataframe2)
'data.frame':   24 obs. of  6 variables:
 $ Date        : Date, format: NA NA NA NA ...
 $ All.Patients: num  15.62 6.6 4.29 8.96 3.53 ...
 $ n13under    : num  7.41 0 0 7.38 4.76 ...
 $ n14over     : num  26.19 11.48 7.69 11.39 2.33 ...
 $ n15under    : num  6.56 0 0 6.67 4.17 ...
 $ n16over     : num  31.4 14.6 10.3 13.6 2.7 ...

The first column of data is formatted as date (not character) in the Excel spreadsheet.

Any suggestions how I can read in the non-standard format month/year data with the xlsx package?

Thank you!

Sam

messages.author: 1db601ea1fed90a0
messages.subject: Re: Reading Month/Year data
parts:
Hi Sam, 

As I replied to you in private, you need to figure out if your "Date" column is a Text or a Date in Excel?  I guess it's Text. If you get a factor, you can always convert a factor to a character using as.character().  For read.xlsx2, the column class should be "character" for the first one, not a Date. 

If using read.xlsx, you'll need to construct from the string "07/2012" a Date.  Something like:  
  mydataframe2$month <- as.Date(paste("01/", mydataframe2$Date, sep=""), format="%d/%m/%Y")

Best, 
Adrian
